status_as_of_cutoff: Local process. Google is publicly identified through Harmony Group LLC, a subsidiary of Google LLC, as the proposed project proposer/owner-operator. Hermantown posted the Final Updated Hermantown Industrial AUAR on August 5, 2026 after submitting it to the Environmental Quality Board on August 4, with EQB Monitor posting expected August 11 and City Council adoption deliberation anticipated in fall 2026. No final special-use permit, CIDP/site-plan approval, building permit, construction start, inspection, CO, final interconnection approval, energization, commissioning, or service record was located.

actions.result_status: The city announced Google's plans for a new Hermantown data center and identified Minnesota Power as the prospective power-grid partner.
actions.access_caveat: City press release identifies a proposal; it is not a final land-use approval or permit.

actions.result_status: The city's project page says Minnesota Power presented efforts to create an electric service agreement with Google at the March 16 pre-agenda meeting. No executed agreement, allocation, or energization was located.
actions.access_caveat: Page summary does not publish the presentation or an executed service agreement.
actions.evidence_note: Utility planning context, not a service or power-on record.

actions.result_status: The city opened public comment on an updated AUAR scoping document for the proposed Google data-center campus.
actions.case_or_ordinance_permit_number: AUAR scoping document; number not published in reviewed notice
actions.access_caveat: Scoping/comment notice is not a final AUAR, rezoning, permit, or construction approval.

actions.government_body: Hermantown City Council (reported by Northern News Now)
actions.result_status: Local reporting says the council approved reimbursement to Minnesota Power for transmission environmental-review work; the report does not establish final data-center approval or construction.
actions.case_or_ordinance_permit_number: Reimbursement agreement; number not exposed in reviewed report
actions.access_caveat: Secondary report; underlying council agenda/minutes/agreement were not retrieved.
actions.evidence_note: Government action reported by local media and explicitly not upgraded to project approval.

actions.action_type: AUAR scoping acceptance / order to prepare draft AUAR
actions.result_status: City AUAR materials state the scoping document was accepted and preparation of the AUAR authorized on May 18, 2026.
actions.access_caveat: Official work-session presentation summarizes the prior council action; underlying May 18 packet is linked from the city project page.
actions.evidence_note: Environmental-review process milestone, not land-use approval.

actions.action_type: Draft AUAR and mitigation-plan comment period
actions.result_status: The city opened a second public comment period focused on the Draft AUAR and associated Mitigation Plan, with comments due July 16, 2026.
actions.case_or_ordinance_permit_number: Updated Hermantown Industrial Draft AUAR and Mitigation Plan
actions.access_caveat: Comment-period notice is not a final AUAR adoption, permit, or construction authorization.

actions.government_body: City of Hermantown / Minnesota Environmental Quality Board
actions.action_type: Final Updated AUAR submitted to EQB
actions.result_status: The city project page says the Final Updated Hermantown Industrial AUAR was submitted to EQB on August 4, 2026 and would be posted to the EQB Monitor on August 11, 2026; the July 27 work-session presentation said council deliberation/adoption was anticipated in fall 2026.
actions.access_caveat: Final AUAR submission/posting does not itself approve the project; city adoption and subsequent permits remain pending in reviewed records.
actions.evidence_note: Official municipal project page updated August 5, 2026.

actions.result_status: The Final Updated AUAR identifies the proposer as Harmony Group LLC, a subsidiary of Google LLC, and evaluates a 278-acre, 26-parcel study area with up to four one-story data-center buildings, one warehouse, two office buildings, and 1.8 million square feet of data-center, warehouse, storage, and office development. It states the data-center use requires a Special Use Permit in the Business and Light Manufacturing District, and that preliminary construction is anticipated no earlier than 2027 and depends on permitting approvals.
actions.access_caveat: AUAR maximum-build scenario and anticipated timing are planning assumptions, not evidence of permit issuance or construction start.
